notes.text: “Grants” is our grouping: federal money and the state’s program grants, less school-meal money, which is paid per meal by formula. Chapter 70, transport aid and pensions the state pays are left out.
Monty Tech’s own chart shows $3,681,900 in grant awards for FY2025: awards in a later year, not revenue received.

notes.text: Lunenburg reported no school-meal revenue to the survey, where Monty Tech reported $1,266,000 of federal meal money. If Lunenburg’s sits in another federal line, its grant share is overstated.

conclusions.text: Grants and donations were 7.7% of Monty Tech’s revenue and 7.2% of Lunenburg schools’.

notes.text: Money a separate foundation or booster club raises and spends itself is not on a district’s books, so it is not in either figure.

views.label: Dollars
lines: Paid by other school systems (D11): the form asks for “payments received from other school systems, both within and outside the state, for tuition, transportation, and other services”, and tells a regional district to report here any assessments paid by independent school districts.
Tuition (A07): the Census item is “Tuition fees from pupils, parents, and other private sources”, one of the form’s student-fee lines. Tuition another school system pays is D11, not this.
School meal sales (A09): what students, teachers and adults paid for breakfasts, lunches and milk, “not from state or federal funds”; those are the school-meal row above.
Student activity receipts (A13): gross receipts of district activity funds “under control of the custodian of district funds”.

Rent (A40): the Census item is “Rents and royalties”; the form asks for revenue “from allowing temporary possession or granting rights to the use of school district buildings, land, or other properties”.
Interest earned (U22): “interest earnings from all funds held by the school system”, every fund, not the general fund alone.
Refunds and other local revenue (U97): “receipts from refunds of prior year expenditures and other revenue from local sources not provided for elsewhere”. The survey does not split the two.

What Monty Tech’s tuition (A07), payments from other school systems (D11) and refunds and other revenue (U97) were for is not in any document held here. Its FY2024 budget book lists Practical Nursing and Continuing and Post Graduate Studies staff among those paid from revolving or special-revenue funds, so those programmes exist; it prints no revenue for them. Closes: Monty Tech’s audited financial statements, revenue by fund.
views.note: Census Bureau. Town budgets: for Lunenburg, the Town of Lunenburg’s appropriation; for Monty Tech, what its member towns are assessed. The file reports thousands of dollars, shown here times 1,000; each total is checked against its items. The rows after town budgets are the rest of local revenue, one row per Census item; an item neither district reported is left out.
